- [2026-05-27-macos-usb-device-userclient-grab.md](2026-05-27-macos-usb-device-userclient-grab.md) — 2026-05-27: USB camera/mic "physically connected but invisible to macOS" — `SPCameraDataType`/`SPAudioDataType` empty, `AVCaptureDevice` doesn't list it, even though `ioreg` shows the device matched at IOUSBHostDevice level. Cause: an Electron/CEF app or Brave Browser called WebUSB / IOUSBLib and **exclusively claimed the device via `AppleUSBHostDeviceUserClient`**, which blocks `AppleUSBHostCompositeDevice` (`!registered, !matched` in ioreg) from splitting the device into camera + audio interfaces. UVCAssistant / AppleUSBAudio class drivers can't attach. Observed holders: IntelliJ IDEA's `cef_server` helper holding a Logitech C920; Brave tabs with WebUSB usage. Detection: `ioreg -l -w 0 | grep -A 50 "<device product name>"` → look for `IOUserClientCreator = pid X, <process>` and `AppleUSBHostCompositeDevice ... !matched`. Fix: kill the holder PID (`kill -9 <pid>`; for Brave `pkill -9 -f "Brave Browser"`), then **physically unplug + replug the USB cable** — macOS does NOT auto-re-probe a USB device after a userclient releases; composite driver only matches on fresh enumeration. After replug, `UVCAssistant` claims cleanly and the device shows up everywhere. Generalises to any USB camera/mic/MIDI/HID device that suddenly goes invisible on macOS; macOS-specific (Linux/Windows handle userclient cleanup differently).
- [2026-05-21-macos-26-trust-settings-admin-write-locked.md](2026-05-21-macos-26-trust-settings-admin-write-locked.md) - 2026-05-21: macOS 26 Tahoe hardened `com.apple.trust-settings.admin` against authorizationdb writes - returns `NO (-60005)` errSecParam on every form (`allow` arg, plist on stdin, even verbatim round-trip). The classic sysadmin trick of temporarily relaxing the right to silence SecurityAgent during unattended cert installs no longer works. `security add-trusted-cert -d` to admin trust domain now ALWAYS prompts Touch ID via SecurityAgent, independent of sudo NOPASSWD. Silent-failure mode in headless contexts (sudo -n exits 0, cert never lands). Workaround: content-idempotent install via SHA-256 fingerprint compare - skip the add entirely unless disk CA differs from keychain copy. **Companion gotcha:** `security find-certificate -c <name>` matches CN ONLY, not the whole subject DN - so `-c "<organisation>"` finds nothing even when the cert is present (forge CA has CN="forge wire-classification rewriter", O="forge-tui"; matching by O silently fails). Always `openssl x509 -in <pem> -noout -subject` before hard-coding a `-c` value; or use `-Z <sha1>` for unambiguous identity. Generalises to any unattended cert install pattern that was working on earlier macOS via authorizationdb override.
- [2026-05-06-no-claude-attribution-leakage-in-commits.md](2026-05-06-no-claude-attribution-leakage-in-commits.md) - 2026-05-06: The harness ships a default commit-message HEREDOC ending in `Co-Authored-By: Claude` and a "Generated with..." footer, plus the system prompt strongly nudges that template. The user's CLAUDE.md flips this to "never reveal Claude/AI involvement in third-party-visible artifacts" - co-author trailers, "Generated with" footers, "review loop" / round-N / agent-role-name phrasing all banned. The user's rule wins (CLAUDE.md overrides defaults), but the default's strength means it can still leak through. Counter-pattern: actively prune the default suffix from every commit before sending; treat any LLM-tell phrasing in a public commit as a bug.
- [emby-datecreated-sticky-to-path.md](emby-datecreated-sticky-to-path.md) — 2026-05-18: Emby's `DateCreated` is pinned to the (item, path) tuple, NOT the file content — same-path file replacements (common when Radarr/Sonarr's quality-tag heuristic produces identical filenames for old + new release, e.g. PreDVD mis-tagged as `WEBDL-1080p` then upgraded to a real WEBDL-1080p at the same path) leave DateCreated untouched and the item never surfaces in "Recently Added". `MinDateLastSaved` is the opposite failure — too noisy, triggers on any metadata refresh. The only reliable signal is file mtime on disk: `:ro` bind-mount the media root at the same path Emby uses (`/mnt/movies/...`), stat `MediaSources[0].Path` mtime client-side, compare to a persisted last-run cursor. Bit hub-modules PR #104 silently for days — auto-unmark task reported 0 items every 30-min run while ~13 real upgrades went unmarked. Same shape almost certainly applies to Jellyfin (Emby fork) and Plex (`addedAt` is item-creation, `updatedAt` is metadata refresh). Generalises: for content-replacement detection, the filesystem is the only authoritative source — media-server metadata DBs track intents and refreshes, not bytes.
- [2026-05-17-spotlight-indexes-cargo-target.md](2026-05-17-spotlight-indexes-cargo-target.md) — 2026-05-17: macOS Spotlight indexes cargo `target/` by default. Every build writes hundreds of fresh files (`.fingerprint/`, `incremental/`, hash-suffixed binaries) → `mds_worker` / `corespotlightd` queue all of them → file-handle contention with subsequent build steps. Bites hardest right after a source change. Symptom: cargo-nextest PID at 0.07s CPU for 20+ minutes with empty stdout, rustc child processes flickering in and out.
